# Session source index

One place to look up everything recorded for each session. **Read-only compilation, not a new authority:** the accepted plan and scope come from `decisions/topic_decisions.yaml`, assignment and video dependencies from their decision files, book and source evidence from `analysis/normalized_topics.yaml`. Edit those and regenerate.

Page numbers are the PDF pages recorded in the evidence. They are used consistently but can differ from PPTX slide numbers where a deck has hidden slides. Evidence shows where a source treats a topic; it is not a vote for inclusion, and a missing source is not evidence that the topic was not taught.

Local decks with no page-level evidence (added or not exported when the evidence was collected); inspect them directly: `0 - NutsAndBolts.pptx`, `12 - Offline RL.pptx`, `7 - Policy Space Methods_old.pptx`, `Project.pptx`.

### 12.2 IQL value/policy fitting and CQL contrast (`offline_constraints`)

- **Teaching:** 59 min (range 54–78); confidence low
- **Requires:** 12.1 `offline_failure`
- **Worked activity:** Expectile example, in-dataset V/Q fitting and advantage-weighted policy extraction; brief CQL contrast and evaluation. Use the existing IQL worked example to map equations to the three scaffolded loss interfaces (estimated 5–8 minutes within that example, not an added block).
- **Pacing note:** IQL uses an upper in-support value estimate, not a generic lower-confidence bound. No full IQL implementation is implied. LSTD is a five-minute optional substitution, not an addition.
- **Segments:** Expectile numerical example (10 min); IQL V/Q fitting without unseen-action maximization (14 min); Advantage-weighted policy extraction (12 min); CQL conservative-penalty contrast (5 min); Trace one IQL update through the shared dataset (10 min); Coverage and evaluation check (8 min)
- **Prerequisite for:** A4 Scaffolded IQL and offline data support (release week 12)

- **Teaching:** 59 min (range 54–72); confidence low

- **Worked activity:** Video retrieval check; formulation, reward-model/online loop, PPO/KL example and policy drift.

Topics referenced by the sessions above, with the sessions that use them.

### Environment models (`environment_models`)

Sessions: 1.1, 1.2, 5.1, 7.1, 11.2.

- **Sutton & Barto:** §8.1 Models and Planning (printed pp. 159–161, [PDF pp. 181–183](../../sources/RLbook2020.pdf#page=181))
- **Current course (local)** (explicitly-covered):
  - [2 - Markov Decision Processes.pdf](../../sources/current_course/2%20-%20Markov%20Decision%20Processes.pdf#page=3) pp. 3–11 (deck: `2 - Markov Decision Processes.pptx`) — Defines histories, Markov state, observability, models and the distinction between learning and planning.
  - [4 - Model Free Prediction.pdf](../../sources/current_course/4%20-%20Model%20Free%20Prediction.pdf#page=7) pp. 7–14 (deck: `4 - Model Free Prediction.pptx`) — Contrasts planning/learning, model-based/model-free and on/off-policy axes; its offline-MDP terminology is not mapped to offline RL.
  - [10 - Model Based RL.pdf](../../sources/current_course/10%20-%20Model%20Based%20RL.pdf#page=3) pp. 3–18 (deck: `10 - Model Based RL.pptx`) — Discusses learned dynamics/reward models, inaccurate models and Dyna pseudocode/examples.

  - [lecture-8-integrating-learning-and-planning.pdf](https://davidstarsilver.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/04/lecture-8-integrating-learning-and-planning.pdf#page=10) pp. 10–20 — Explains model fitting and planning with inaccurate learned models.
  - [previous-rl-exam-questions-.pdf](https://davidstarsilver.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/04/previous-rl-exam-questions-.pdf#page=3) p. 3 — Past exam asks for MC, batch TD, trace-based TD and LSTD estimates on observed episodes.
- **CS285** (explicitly-covered):
  - [lec-4.pdf](https://rail.eecs.berkeley.edu/deeprlcourse/static/slides/lec-4.pdf#page=18) pp. 18–38 — Develops RL algorithm structure, values and policy/model/data-use distinctions.
